answer_text: On a Cisco Catalyst 9300, set the switch port connected to the Cato Socket as an 802.1Q trunk and allow the VLANs you need. Make sure the VLAN IDs (VIDs) on the switch match the VLANs configured on the Socket; you can configure the CMA native range to a specific VLAN ID if desired. Ensure the native VLAN behavior is consistent on both sides (untagged vs tagged). Depending on your mapping, the native range can be left untagged on the trunk (native VLAN) or tagged on the trunk and mapped to the Socket's native range.
